## Overview

Implements RFC #64039. Pooling requests served through an IO Processor plugin can now run pre-processing, inference and post-processing (IO) as separate stages on different instances. The PR adds three endpoints and an `IOConnector` framework that moves tensors directly between instances. Pre- and post-processing can then run on GPU-less `vllm launch render` instances and scale separately from the GPU inference instance.

> **Draft:** opened to collect design feedback alongside the RFC. Unit tests and docs are not included yet (see [Before ready for review](#before-ready-for-review)). The six commits are self-contained, and we are happy to split them into a PR series as the RFC proposes.

## Claims

- New endpoints:
  - `POST /pooling/preprocess` (`vllm launch render`): runs `IOProcessor.pre_process()` and returns one `GeneratePoolingRequest` per rendered item.
  - `POST /pooling/inference` (`vllm serve`): fetches the pre-processed `MultiModalKwargsItem`, runs the pooling model and returns a `GeneratePoolingResponse` that references the output tensor.
  - `POST /pooling/postprocess` (`vllm launch render`): fetches the output tensors and per-request metadata, then runs `IOProcessor.post_process()`.
- New `IOTransferConfig` / `--io-transfer-config`, modelled on `KVTransferConfig` and `ECTransferConfig`.
- New `IOConnectorBase` with `put_data` / `get_data` / `cleanup_data` and `put_metadata` / `get_metadata` / `cleanup_metadata`, each with an async variant. Two built-in backends:
  - `IOExampleConnector`: shared filesystem (e.g. a PVC).
  - `IOP2PConnector`: ZMQ ROUTER/DEALER, pull-based, sends tensor buffers as zero-copy frames.
- New `IOProcessor.get_request_metadata()` / `update_request_metadata()` hooks with no-op defaults, so request state saved during pre-processing can be restored on a different post-processing instance.
- Without a connector, the endpoints still work: payloads are sent inline in the JSON body (base64 msgpack).
- Existing endpoints are unchanged. All new behaviour is opt-in through `--io-transfer-config` and the new routes.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD`: all hooks pass, including ruff, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-imports, root-lazy-imports and config-validation.
- End to end using TerraTorch Prithvi-EO-2.0 segmentation (8 pre, 1 inference, 8 post instances). Performance results are summarized in the RFC (#64039).

## Details

### Request flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Router
  participant PRE as Preprocess (vllm launch render)
  participant INF as Inference (vllm serve)
  participant POST as Postprocess (vllm launch render)

  S->>PRE: POST /pooling/preprocess (IOProcessorRequest)
  PRE-->>PRE: IOProcessor.pre_process + render
  PRE-->>PRE: put_data(mm item), put_metadata(request state)
  PRE->>S: [GeneratePoolingRequest{data_ref, metadata_ref}]
  S->>INF: POST /pooling/inference (one per item)
  INF-->>PRE: get_data(data_ref)
  INF-->>INF: encode()
  INF-->>INF: put_data(output tensor)
  INF->>S: GeneratePoolingResponse{output_data_ref, metadata_ref}
  S->>POST: POST /pooling/postprocess (all responses)
  POST-->>INF: get_data(output_data_ref)
  POST-->>PRE: get_metadata(metadata_ref)
  POST-->>POST: update_request_metadata + IOProcessor.post_process
  POST->>S: IOProcessorResponse
```

### Commits

Each commit can be reviewed on its own and maps to one PR in the series proposed in the RFC.

1. **`[Config] Add IOTransferConfig`**: adds `IOTransferConfig` and `--io-transfer-config`, modelled on `KVTransferConfig`/`ECTransferConfig`. It validates `io_role`, supports `io_connector_module_path` for custom connectors, and is included in the `VllmConfig` hash.
2. **`[Plugin] Add IOProcessor request metadata hooks`**: adds `get_request_metadata` / `update_request_metadata` with no-op defaults. Plugins use them to export state saved during `pre_process` and restore it on a different post-processing instance.
3. **`[Frontend] Add disaggregated pooling protocol`**: adds `DataRef`, `MetadataRef`, `DataObject`, `GeneratePoolingRequest`/`GeneratePoolingResponse` and `PostProcessPoolingRequest`. Also adds base64 msgpack tensor encoding, used when no IO connector is configured.
4. **`[Distributed] Add IO connector framework`**: adds `IOConnectorBase` with sync and async put/get/cleanup for data and metadata, and a lazy-loading connector factory. Also adds process-wide state that owns the connector and a dedicated IO thread pool. Built-in backends: `IOExampleConnector` (shared filesystem) and `IOP2PConnector` (ZMQ ROUTER/DEALER, zero-copy tensor frames).
5. **`[Frontend] Add /pooling/inference endpoint`**: fetches the pre-processed multimodal item through the IO connector or from the request body, runs `encode()`, stores the output tensor and returns references to it. The API server shuts the IO connector down on exit.
6. **`[Frontend] Add pooling pre/postprocess to render server`**: runs the IO processor plugin on GPU-less render instances. `/pooling/preprocess` stores each rendered item and its request metadata through the IO connector. `/pooling/postprocess` fetches the output tensors and metadata, then runs `post_process`. Connector calls use the dedicated IO thread pool.

### Design notes

- **References, not payloads.** Requests and responses carry a `DataRef` (`object_id` plus a `locator`) and a `MetadataRef`. The connector moves the data. This follows the `mm_hashes` pattern: the pre-processing `mm_hash` becomes the `object_id`, and the inference output is stored as `<mm_hash>:<served_model_name>:output`.
- **Metadata is keyed by request, data by object.** The same data object can be reused across requests whose metadata differs.
- **One connector per process.** `vllm.distributed.io_transfer` owns the connector (its role comes from `io_role`) and creates it once per process, as the EC/KV transfer state modules do. Both `vllm serve` and `vllm launch render` shut it down on exit.
- **Dedicated IO thread pool.** On render instances, connector calls run on a separate thread pool sized by `io_connector_extra_config.max_io_threads`, so blocking IO does not use renderer workers. Inference instances reuse the renderer executor.
- **Connector serialization** uses `MsgpackEncoder`/`MsgpackDecoder` from `vllm.v1.serial_utils` for payloads and `msgspec.msgpack` for envelopes and metadata. No new dependencies are added.
- **Custom connectors** can be loaded with `io_connector_module_path`, like `kv_connector_module_path`.

### Limitations / follow-ups

- Only full three-stage disaggregation is supported. Partial setups, such as co-locating inference and post-processing, are not.
- Each prompt must contain exactly one `image` item (enough for TerraTorch). `/pooling/preprocess` rejects other inputs with a 400 error.
- `IOP2PConnector` is functional, but its performance under high load still needs tuning compared with the shared-storage connector.

### Before ready for review

- [ ] Unit tests: `IOTransferConfig` validation, round trips for both connectors, and the three routes with a dummy IO processor plugin (CPU only, using the filesystem connector).
- [ ] Docs in `docs/` and an example deployment under `examples/`.
- [ ] Address RFC feedback (#64039). That may include splitting this into the PR series described there.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""IOConnectorBase — abstract base for transferring IO data
+between disaggregated vLLM roles (preprocessor / worker / postprocessor).
+
+The interface mirrors ECConnectorBase but is oriented around
+per-request IO data rather than encoder-cache tensors:
+
+    put_data(object_id, data, metadata) -> DataRef  – called by the sender role
+    get_data(ref) -> DataObject                     – called by the receiver role
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+import enum
+from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
+from concurrent.futures import Executor
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import IOTransferConfig, VllmConfig
+    from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.pooling.protocol import (
+        DataObject,
+        DataRef,
+        MetadataRef,
+    )
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class IOConnectorRole(enum.Enum):
+    # Can only send IO data, e.g. the preprocessing instance
+    SENDER = 0
+    # Can only receive IO data, e.g. the postprocessing instance
+    RECEIVER = 1
+    # Can send and receive IO data, e.g. the inference instance
+    BOTH = 2
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_config(cls, io_transfer_config: "IOTransferConfig") -> "IOConnectorRole":
+        if io_transfer_config.is_io_sender and io_transfer_config.is_io_receiver:
+            return cls.BOTH
+        if io_transfer_config.is_io_sender:
+            return cls.SENDER
+        return cls.RECEIVER
+
+
+class IOConnectorBase(ABC):
+    """Abstract base class for IO data transfer connectors.
+
+    Subclasses implement the storage / transport backend
+    (shared filesystem, object store, in-memory bus, …).
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, vllm_config: "VllmConfig", role: IOConnectorRole) -> None:
+        self._vllm_config = vllm_config
+        self._role = role
+        cfg = vllm_config.io_transfer_config
+        if cfg is None:
+            raise ValueError("io_transfer_config must be set for IOConnectorBase")
+        self._is_io_sender: bool = cfg.is_io_sender
+        self._is_io_receiver: bool = cfg.is_io_receiver
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Properties
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    @property
+    def role(self) -> IOConnectorRole:
+        return self._role
+
+    @property
+    def is_io_sender(self) -> bool:
+        """True when this instance sends IO data."""
+        return self._is_io_sender
+
+    @property
+    def is_io_receiver(self) -> bool:
+        """True when this instance receives IO data."""
+        return self._is_io_receiver
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # Lifecycle
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+

+"""Example IO connector that stores/loads base64-encoded files on a shared filesystem.
+
+This is intentionally simple — suitable for debugging and single-node
+setups — and mirrors the structure of ECExampleConnector.
+"""

+import os
+import struct
+import threading
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+
+from vllm.distributed.io_transfer.io_connector.base import (
+    IOConnectorBase,
+    IOConnectorRole,
+)
+from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.pooling.protocol import (
+    DataLocation,
+    DataObject,
+    DataRef,
+    MetadataRef,
+)

+from vllm.multimodal.inputs import MultiModalKwargsItem
+from vllm.v1.serial_utils import MsgpackDecoder, MsgpackEncoder

+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# Allowed payload types and the tag written into the wire envelope.
+# The tag is used on the receive side to pick the right MsgpackDecoder type.
+_TYPE_TAG: dict[type, str] = {
+    MultiModalKwargsItem: "MultiModalKwargsItem",
+    torch.Tensor: "Tensor",
+}
+_TAG_TO_TYPE: dict[str, type] = {v: k for k, v in _TYPE_TAG.items()}
+
+# Thread-local storage for encoder and decoder instances.
+# MsgpackEncoder / MsgpackDecoder are not thread-safe (they use mutable
+# instance state — aux_buffers — during encode/decode), but they are safe to
+# reuse within a single thread sequentially.  Constructing a new Encoder or
+# Decoder on every call is expensive because msgspec compiles the type schema
+# at construction time.  thread-local instances pay that cost once per thread
+# and then reuse the compiled schema on every subsequent call.
+_local = threading.local()
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Wire framing helpers
+#
+# Format written to disk:
+#   [4B LE] number of frames  N
+#   for each frame:
+#     [4B LE] frame length L
+#     [L bytes] frame data
+#
+# Frame 0 is always the UTF-8 type tag.
+# Frames 1..N-1 are the raw buffers returned by MsgpackEncoder.encode().
+#
+# This avoids re-packing all tensor side-buffers into a single merged
+# allocation; writelines() issues a writev()-style write for each chunk.
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _pack_frames(tag: str, bufs: list) -> list:
+    """Return iovec-style chunks for writelines() — no buffer merging."""
+    tag_bytes = tag.encode()
+    n_frames = 1 + len(bufs)
+    header = struct.pack("<I", n_frames)
+    tag_frame = struct.pack("<I", len(tag_bytes)) + tag_bytes
+    chunks: list = [header, tag_frame]
+    for b in bufs:
+        b = bytes(b)  # materialise memoryview without a second copy
+        chunks.append(struct.pack("<I", len(b)))
+        chunks.append(b)
+    return chunks
+
+
+def _unpack_frames(raw: bytes) -> tuple[str, list[bytes]]:
+    """Inverse of _pack_frames — O(n_frames) with no extra allocation."""
+    pos = 0
+    (n_frames,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, pos)
+    pos += 4
+    frames: list[bytes] = []
+    for _ in range(n_frames):
+        (length,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, pos)
+        pos += 4
+        frames.append(raw[pos : pos + length])
+        pos += length
+    if not frames:
+        raise ValueError("IOExampleConnector: empty frame list in payload")
+    tag = frames[0].decode()
+    return tag, frames[1:]
+
+
+def _get_encoder() -> MsgpackEncoder:
+    enc = getattr(_local, "encoder", None)
+    if enc is None:
+        enc = MsgpackEncoder()
+        _local.encoder = enc
+    return enc
+
+
+def _get_decoder(tag: str) -> MsgpackDecoder:
+    decoders: dict[str, MsgpackDecoder] = getattr(_local, "decoders", None) or {}
+    dec = decoders.get(tag)
+    if dec is None:

+                "(is_io_sender=False). Check your io_transfer_config."
+            )

+        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as f:
+            f.writelines(chunks)

+

+        self.created_data_refs.append(data_ref)
+

+
+    def get_data(
+        self,
+        ref: DataRef,
+    ) -> DataObject:
+        """Read and deserialize the file referenced by *ref* using MsgpackDecoder.
+
+        Returns:
+            The ``DataObject`` stored by the corresponding ``put_data`` call.
+
+        Raises:
+            RuntimeError: If this connector is not configured as a receiver.
+            KeyError: If no file exists at the path recorded in *ref*.
+
+        """
+        if not self.is_io_receiver:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "This IOExampleConnector is not configured as a receiver "
+                "(is_io_receiver=False). Check your io_transfer_config."
+            )
+
+        filepath = os.path.join(self._storage_path, f"{ref.object_id}.msg")
+
+        # Single open() — no preceding exists() stat(), no TOCTOU race.
+        try:
+            with open(filepath, "rb") as f:
+                raw_bytes = f.read()
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            raise KeyError(
+                f"No IO transfer payload found for object_id={ref.object_id!r} "
+                f"(expected at {filepath})"
+            ) from None
+

+        decoder = _get_decoder(tag)
+        data = decoder.decode(frames)
+
+        return DataObject(data=data)
+
+    def cleanup_data(self, ref: DataRef) -> None:
+        """Delete the file written by ``put_data`` for *ref*.
+
+        A no-op when the file has already been removed.
+
+        Raises:
+            RuntimeError: If this connector is not configured as a sender.
+
+        """
+        filepath = os.path.join(self._storage_path, f"{ref.object_id}.msg")
+        try:
+            os.remove(filepath)
+            logger.debug("Removed IO data file %s", filepath)
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            pass
+
+    def put_metadata(
+        self,
+        request_id: str,
+        metadata: dict,
+    ) -> MetadataRef:
+        """Write per-request *metadata* to ``<storage_path>/<request_id>.meta``."""
+        if not self.is_io_sender:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "This IOExampleConnector is not configured as a sender "
+                "(is_io_sender=False). Check your io_transfer_config."
+            )
+        filepath = os.path.join(self._storage_path, f"{request_id}.meta")
+        with open(filepath, "wb") as f:
+            packed_metadata = msgspec.msgpack.encode(metadata)
+            f.write(packed_metadata)
+        logger.debug("Saved metadata for request_id=%s", request_id)
+
+        return MetadataRef(
+            request_id=request_id,
+            location=DataLocation(locator=filepath),
+        )
+
+    def get_metadata(
+        self,
+        ref: MetadataRef,
+    ) -> dict:
+        """Read per-request metadata from ``<storage_path>/<request_id>.meta``."""
+        if not self.is_io_receiver:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "This IOExampleConnector is not configured as a receiver "
+                "(is_io_receiver=False). Check your io_transfer_config."
+            )
+        filepath = ref.location.locator
+        if not os.path.exists(filepath):
+            return {}
+        with open(filepath, "rb") as f:
+            result = msgspec.msgpack.decode(f.read())
+        if not isinstance(result, dict):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "IOExampleConnector: corrupt metadata for "
+                f"request_id={ref.request_id!r}: expected a dict, "
+                f"got {type(result).__name__!r}"
+            )
+        return result
+
+    def cleanup_metadata(self, ref: "MetadataRef") -> None:
+        """Delete the metadata file for *ref.request_id*."""
+        filepath = os.path.join(self._storage_path, f"{ref.request_id}.meta")
+        try:
+            os.remove(filepath)
+            logger.debug("Removed metadata file %s", filepath)
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            pass
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        for data_ref in self.created_data_refs:
+            self.cleanup_data(data_ref)
+        self.created_data_refs = []

+import importlib

+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from vllm.distributed.io_transfer.io_connector.base import (

+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class IOConnectorFactory:
+    """Registry + factory for :class:`IOConnectorBase` implementations.
+
+    Connectors are registered lazily so their modules are only imported
+    when the connector is actually instantiated.
+    """
+
+    _registry: dict[str, Callable[[], type[IOConnectorBase]]] = {}
+
+    @classmethod
+    def register_connector(
+        cls,
+        name: str,
+        module_path: str,
+        class_name: str,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Register a connector with a lazy-loading module and class name."""
+        if name in cls._registry:
+            raise ValueError(f"IO connector '{name}' is already registered.")
+
+        def loader() -> type[IOConnectorBase]:
+            module = importlib.import_module(module_path)
+            return getattr(module, class_name)
+
+        cls._registry[name] = loader
+
+    @classmethod
+    def create_connector(
+        cls,
+        config: "VllmConfig",
+        role: IOConnectorRole,
+    ) -> IOConnectorBase:
+        """Instantiate the configured connector."""
+        io_transfer_config = config.io_transfer_config
+        if io_transfer_config is None:
+            raise ValueError("io_transfer_config must be set to create an IO connector")
+        connector_cls = cls.get_connector_class(io_transfer_config)
+        logger.info(
+            "Creating IO connector %s (engine_id=%s)",
+            connector_cls.__name__,
+            io_transfer_config.engine_id,
+        )
+        return connector_cls(config, role)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_connector_class(
+        cls,
+        io_transfer_config: "IOTransferConfig",
+    ) -> type[IOConnectorBase]:
+        """Resolve the connector class by name."""
+        connector_name = io_transfer_config.io_connector
+        if connector_name is None:
+            raise ValueError("io_connector must not be None")
+        if connector_name in cls._registry:
+            return cls._registry[connector_name]()
+        # Fall back to dynamic import via explicit module path.
+        module_path = io_transfer_config.io_connector_module_path
+        if module_path is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Unsupported IO connector type: {connector_name!r}. "
+                "Set io_connector_module_path to load a custom connector."
+            )
+        module = importlib.import_module(module_path)
+        return getattr(module, connector_name)
+

+# Built-in connector registrations

+------------
+  * ``put_data()`` (sender side) is non-blocking: it encodes the payload
+    using MsgpackEncoder (which yields a header buffer + zero or more
+    tensor backing-memory views) and stores all buffers in the engine's
+    local send buffer, then immediately returns a ``DataRef`` encoding the
+    sender's own address.

+    ``DataRef`` to issue a GET request to the sender's engine, which
+    serves the buffered buffers on demand.  MsgpackDecoder reconstructs
+    the original object from the received buffers using the type tag stored
+    in the wire envelope.

+    engine if the receiver never calls get_data().

+--------------
+MsgpackEncoder encodes the payload into a list of buffers:
+  bufs[0]   — msgpack header (small, inlined metadata + tensor shape/dtype)
+  bufs[1:]  — direct memoryview pointers into each tensor's backing storage

+These buffers are handed to the engine, which sends each one as a separate
+ZMQ frame with ``zmq.Frame(buf, copy=False)``.  ZMQ holds a reference to
+the backing memory and puts it on the wire without an additional memcpy.
+
+On the receive side the frame bytes are fed directly to MsgpackDecoder
+with ``share_mem=True`` (the default), so tensors are reconstructed as
+views over the received bytes rather than copying them again.

+    put_object(object_id, frames)
+    fetch_object(object_id, remote_address) -> list[bytes] | None   [sync]

+"""P2pEngine — ZMQ-based byte-transfer engine for IO connector.
+
+Transfers arbitrary bytes between disaggregated vLLM roles using a
+ZMQ ROUTER/DEALER pattern.
+
+Protocol (GET mode)
+-------------------
+The sender buffers objects locally. The receiver pulls them on demand.
+
+  put_object(object_id, frames)          — stores a list of buffers in send_store
+                                           (non-blocking)
+  fetch_object(object_id, sender_addr)   — receiver sends GET, awaits reply without
+                                           blocking the calling thread or the main
+                                           event loop; returns list[bytes]
+  delete_object(object_id)               — sender discards a buffered object
+
+Wire protocol for fetch_object:
+  Receiver DEALER → Sender ROUTER  :
+    frame 0: msgpack {"cmd": "GET", "object_id": <id>, "correlation_id": <int>}
+
+  Sender ROUTER → Receiver DEALER (success):
+    frame 0: msgpack {"ok": True,  "correlation_id": <int>, "num_frames": N}
+    frame 1..N: raw payload buffers (each sent with copy=False)
+
+  Sender ROUTER → Receiver DEALER (error):
+    frame 0: msgpack {"ok": False, "error": <str>, "correlation_id": <int>}
+
+Each payload buffer is a separate ZMQ frame.  The envelope (frame 0) stays
+small and cheap to encode; the payload frames are passed to
+``send_multipart`` with ``zmq.Frame(..., copy=False)`` so ZMQ references the
+backing buffers directly without an additional memcpy.
+
+Correlation ID
+--------------
+Every fetch_object call generates a unique ``correlation_id`` from a
+per-connection monotonic integer counter.  The ID is sent in the request
+(as a msgpack integer — more compact than a string) and echoed back in the
+reply.  A persistent reader loop on the async event loop receives all
+incoming replies on the shared DEALER socket and dispatches each one to the
+waiting asyncio.Future via the pending dict keyed by ``correlation_id``.
+
+Socket pool
+-----------
+A single persistent ``zmq.asyncio`` DEALER socket is kept open per
+``remote_address``.  All concurrent ``fetch_object`` calls to the same
+remote are multiplexed over that one socket without any per-request
+connection setup (no TCP handshake, no ZMTP negotiation after the first
+call). Sockets are created lazily on first use and reused for the
+lifetime of the engine.
+
+Non-blocking design
+-------------------
+``fetch_object`` is synchronous on the outside (the ``IOConnectorBase``
+interface does not require async).  Internally the ZMQ send/recv uses
+``zmq.asyncio`` DEALER sockets so the OS thread is never blocked on I/O.
+
+To bridge the sync interface with the async implementation, P2pEngine owns a
+private asyncio event loop that runs permanently in a dedicated daemon thread
+(``_async_loop_thread``).  Each ``fetch_object`` call dispatches
+``_fetch_object_async`` onto that loop via
+``asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`` and blocks only on the returned
+``concurrent.futures.Future``, not on the ZMQ socket.
+
+Single async context
+--------------------
+Both the server-side ROUTER and the client-side DEALER pool share the same
+``zmq.asyncio.Context`` and the same private event loop.  A single daemon
+thread runs the loop; no separate listener thread is needed.  The ROUTER
+receive loop (``_serve``) and each connection's reply reader
+(``_reply_reader``) are all asyncio Tasks on that loop, so the OS scheduler
+never has to wake more than one thread to handle I/O.
+
+Performance notes
+-----------------
+* ZMQ context is created with ``io_threads=2`` so the ZMQ I/O thread pool
+  can keep up with high-bandwidth tensor transfers.  Tune upward for
+  aggregate throughputs above ~10 Gb/s.
+* A single ``msgspec.msgpack.Encoder`` instance is reused for all encode calls,
+  avoiding per-call temporary dict allocations.
+* ``_serve`` processes each GET request inline (no ``create_task`` per
+  request) and attempts a ``NOBLOCK`` send first; only falling back to the
+  async send when the kernel send buffer is momentarily full.
+* ``_send_store`` is mutated exclusively on the async event-loop thread
+  (all external writers route through ``run_coroutine_threadsafe``), so no
+  ``threading.Lock`` is needed.
+* Correlation IDs are plain integers throughout (msgpack int is smaller
+  than msgpack str); the pending dict uses ``int`` keys.
+* ``asyncio.Future`` is resolved directly with ``list[bytes] | None``
+  rather than an intermediate ``(envelope, payload_frames)`` tuple.
